terms.meaning: The markup language web pages are written in.
Replacing characters such as angle brackets with safe codes so that text is shown rather than read as markup.
Named values for colors, fonts, and spacing that styles reuse.

depends_on: assets/design-tokens.css, according to the file header
Python standard library modules argparse, json, html, pathlib, and datetime

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header rules and imports
sections.what: States that slides must take all colors, fonts, and spacing from the token variables, then imports the standard tools for reading arguments, JSON, escaping, file paths, and dates.
sections.why: The header records the design rule, and the imports provide the tools the slide code needs.
sections.watch_out: Nothing visible here enforces the no hard-coded styles rule, so a new hard-coded value would not be caught.

sections.name: _e
sections.title: Escaping text for slides
sections.what: Converts a value into text that is safe to place inside a slide, replacing special characters with harmless codes. A missing value becomes an empty string.
sections.why: Prevents slide text from being read as markup, which could break a slide or inject unwanted content.
sections.watch_out: Only values passed through this helper are protected, so any value inserted without it is not.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 1)
sections.title: Safe link check and output paths
sections.what: Allows links only if they start with http, https, a hash for a page anchor, or a slash for a site path, and escapes them for safe use in HTML. Any other link, such as a script link, is replaced by a plain hash placeholder. It also records where the design token files and the output folder are.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops harmful script links from being placed into slide buttons, as the code's comment notes.
sections.watch_out: Output and token paths are calculated from this file's location, so moving the script breaks where it reads and writes.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 2)
sections.title: Slide style rules for layout and text
sections.what: Holds the page style rules for the slide frame, background variants, glow effect, and heading and body text sizes. These rules are written into every generated deck.
sections.why: Colors and sizes come from the shared design token variables, so the look stays consistent with the brand.
sections.watch_out: The page template is a Python text string where every curly brace must be doubled, so a single brace will break the whole page.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 3)
sections.title: Slide style rules for cards and buttons
sections.what: Holds the style rules for text colors, card boxes, and the base button look, all taken from design token variables.
sections.why: Keeps cards and buttons consistent across all slide types.
sections.watch_out: Same doubled-brace rule applies, because these rules sit inside the page template string.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 4)
sections.title: Slide style rules for button variants and grid
sections.what: Holds the style rules for primary and secondary buttons, simple layout helpers such as flex and grid columns, spacing helpers, and metric number styles.
sections.why: Gives every slide the same layout helpers and button styles.
sections.watch_out: The grid helpers only offer two to four columns, so a slide that needs more must add its own style.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 5)
sections.title: Slide style rules for feature list and quotes
sections.what: Holds the style rules for feature rows with icons, and for testimonial quote boxes and their author lines.
sections.why: Keeps feature and testimonial slides looking the same across decks.
sections.watch_out: Same doubled-brace rule applies inside the template string.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 6)
sections.title: Slide style rules for badges and bar chart
sections.what: Holds the style rules for small badge labels, the chart container, and the bar chart with its height and label spacing.
sections.why: Keeps chart and badge slides on brand.
sections.watch_out: The bar chart has a fixed height of 200 pixels, so very tall bars may be cut off.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 7)
sections.title: Slide style rules for progress, footer and page shell
sections.what: Holds styles for progress bars, the slide footer, and glow shadows. This section also ends the page template and places the title, stylesheet path and slide content into the page shell.
sections.why: Placeholders for the title, stylesheet path and slides are filled in later by the deck builder.
sections.watch_out: The three placeholder names must match exactly what the deck builder passes in, or the page will show raw placeholder text.

sections.name: _safe_url (part 8)
sections.title: Section divider comment
sections.what: A comment marking where the slide builder functions begin. Nothing runs here.
sections.why: Only a visual label for readers of the file.

sections.name: generate_title_slide
sections.title: Title slide builder
sections.what: Builds the opening slide with a badge, a large gradient title, a subtitle, two buttons, and a footer with company name and date. Missing fields get sample text.
sections.why: Each slide type has its own builder so each layout can change on its own.
sections.watch_out: Missing fields show placeholder text such as Your Title Here, which can reach a real deck by accident.

sections.name: generate_problem_slide
sections.title: Problem slide builder
sections.what: Builds a slide with a headline and exactly three numbered pain point cards, each with a title and description, plus a footer.
sections.why: Follows a Problem, Agitate, Solution style of pitch layout, as the code's note says.
sections.watch_out: Only three pain points are supported, so a fourth entry is silently ignored.

sections.name: generate_solution_slide
sections.title: Solution slide builder
sections.what: Builds a slide with a headline, three feature rows with check marks, and a box on the right with the text Product screenshot or demo.
sections.why: Shows the product's main benefits next to a visual area.
sections.watch_out: The right-hand box is only placeholder text, not a real image, unless someone edits the output.

sections.name: generate_metrics_slide
sections.title: Metrics slide builder
sections.what: Builds a slide with up to four large number cards, each with a value and label. If no metrics are given, it uses sample figures such as 10K+ and 2M dollars.
sections.why: Shows traction numbers in a simple, scannable way.
sections.watch_out: Sample figures will appear if the data leaves out metrics, and they could be mistaken for real results.

sections.name: generate_chart_slide
sections.title: Chart slide builder
sections.what: Builds a slide with a CSS bar chart. Each bar height is set as a percentage from its value, with a label under it and a value above it.
sections.why: Shows trends without needing a charting library.
sections.watch_out: Bar heights are used as given, so a value above 100 makes the bar overflow the chart area.

sections.name: generate_testimonial_slide
sections.title: Testimonial slide builder
sections.what: Builds a social proof slide with a quote, an author name and a role. Missing fields show a sample quote and the name Jane Doe.
sections.why: Shows customer praise in a clear layout.
sections.watch_out: The sample quote and name can look like a real endorsement if they are not replaced.

sections.name: generate_cta_slide
sections.title: Closing call to action slide builder
sections.what: Builds the final slide with a headline, a button linking to cta_url through the safe link check, and a footer with contact and website.
sections.why: Gives the audience a clear next step.
sections.watch_out: The default contact address is a placeholder on example.com, which must be replaced before sharing.

sections.name: generate_deck
sections.title: Deck assembler
sections.what: Goes through the list of slides, picks the matching builder by type name, skips unknown types with a printed warning, and then fills the page template with the title and slides.
sections.why: Turns a list of slide data into one complete web page.
sections.watch_out: The stylesheet path is fixed relative to the output folder, so saving decks somewhere else will break the styles.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Command-line options for demo and JSON input
sections.what: Reads the flags for demo, JSON input, and output file. With the demo flag, it writes a sample ClaudeKit marketing deck into the design assets folder. With a JSON flag, it reads a slide list from a file.
sections.why: Lets someone test the generator quickly or build decks from saved data.
sections.watch_out: The demo content describes a made-up product with sample numbers and must not be published as real.

sections.name: main (part 2)
sections.title: Command-line output and help
sections.what: Writes the JSON-based deck to the chosen output path, or to a file named by date and time in the output folder. If no option is given, it prints the help text.
sections.why: Saves the finished deck where the user wants it.
sections.watch_out: Default file names include only the time to the minute, so two runs in the same minute overwrite each other.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Start-up guard
sections.what: Runs the command-line main function only when this file is started directly, not when another file imports it.
sections.why: Standard Python pattern so the file can be reused as a library.

summary: Builds HTML slides for presentations, with all styling taken from design token variables. Only two of its twenty-one sections were included in this packet, so most slide types and the deck builder are not reviewed.
purpose: Creates slide files that match the brand, using the shared design values instead of hard-coded styles.
why: The header states the rule that every style must come from the token variables, which keeps slides on-brand. The reason for the rule is a design decision stated in the header.
how: The script reads command options, builds the HTML for each slide type, and joins them into a deck. Escaping helper protects text placed into slides. Most of the steps are not in this packet.
inputs: Command line options and slide content. The exact content format is not shown in the packet.
outputs: HTML slide content. Whether it saves a file is not shown in the packet.
risks: A hard-coded color or font added later breaks the rule without any visible check. Only text passed through the escaping helper is protected from being read as markup.
debug: If a slide shows an unexpected color or font, look for a value written directly in the slide code rather than a token variable. If text shows broken markup, check whether that value went through the escaping helper.
